findings.claim: Signed favorable-minus-comparison endpoint contrasts are strongest and most reproducible for pair-distance shell densities at short separations: pair_kernel_1.5 (integrated z 0.562, q 1.5e-4, positive batch fraction 1.0), pair_kernel_2.5 (0.631, q 2.2e-5, 1.0), pair_kernel_3.5 (0.540, q 9.8e-5, 1.0) and pair_kernel_5.0 (0.319, q 3.7e-3, 0.857), while pair_kernel_7.0 is negative (-0.485, q 1.5e-4, positive fraction 0.0). Branch-adjusted raw and adjusted correlations agree in sign and survive multiplicity adjustment (e.g. pair_kernel_1.5 adjusted correlation 0.101, q 0.019; pair_kernel_2.5 0.084, q 0.046). These are selection-enrichment contrasts on a standardized coordinate feature, not absolute geometric descriptors or physical interaction energies.

Shape anisotropy carries a consistent negative signed contrast: shape_yy integrated z -0.513 (q 1.5e-5, positive batch fraction 0.0) and shape_xx -0.495 (q 8.1e-4), with shape_zz -0.183 (q 0.067) and shape_yz -0.212 (q 0.035). The same sign recurs in the per-landmark local_cyy enrichment contrasts across all twenty landmarks (all negative, most q<0.05), and in branch-adjusted shape_yy (raw correlation -0.103, q 2.6e-3; adjusted -0.100, q 0.015). This is a signed coordinate contrast, not a claim that a smaller second moment is a physical quality axis.

Landmark soft-minimum distances and radial shell occupancies show mixed but reproducible signed contrasts: softmin at landmarks 00, 04, 06, 18 and 19 is negative (e.g. landmark_00_softmin -0.481, q 8.1e-4; landmark_06_softmin 0.294, q 6.8e-4; landmark_18_softmin 0.264, q 6.0e-3), while occupancy3/occupancy5 at landmarks 00, 02, 05, 06, 15 and 18 are negative (e.g. landmark_06_occupancy5 -0.365, q 6.8e-4; landmark_15_occupancy5 -0.357, q 2.6e-3). The occupancy features are radial shell densities peaking at 3 A and 5 A, not atom counts within a radius, and softmin is a normalized soft minimum distance; neither establishes a quality benefit by itself.

Global centroid coordinates carry weak and largely non-reproducible signed contrasts: global_centroid_y integrated z -0.243 (q 0.014, positive batch fraction 0.214) but global_centroid_x -0.111 (q 0.257) and global_centroid_z -0.061 (q 0.481); branch-adjusted raw and adjusted correlations for all three centroid components are small and mostly non-significant (e.g. adjusted centroid_x -0.010, q 0.70). Centroid contrasts are therefore not a reliable direction on this evidence.

Joint-motion diagnostics are the most reproducible negative contrasts in the branch-adjusted tables: joint_innovation_RMS_A (raw correlation -0.142, q 9.3e-5, positive batch fraction 1.0; adjusted -0.150, q 2.8e-4), joint_internal_RMS_A (raw -0.130, q 1.5e-4, 1.0; adjusted -0.137, q 9.7e-4) and joint_translation_RMS_A (raw -0.067, q 0.087; adjusted -0.076, q 0.052). These are adjusted branch-covariance diagnostics of joint motion, not rigid-motion residuals of the region moments themselves and not atom velocities.

Within-selector joint diagnostics show that selection innovation is positively associated with native alignment (0.092, q 2.2e-9, positive batch fraction 1.0) and with teacher innovation-contrast alignment (0.226, q 2.2e-9, 1.0), but negatively associated with observed child score gain (-0.036, q 1.8e-7, positive batch fraction 0.0). The teacher contrast is predominantly internal (internal fraction 0.787) with smaller translation (0.132) and rotation (0.081) fractions. These are descriptive within-selector associations with batch as the independent unit, not causal selection effects.

The supplied continuous contrast functions are observed-node linear interpolants over the complete observed window [0.0, 0.49] with no extrapolation allowed and no accepted polynomial fit (polynomial_accepted false throughout). They exhibit many sign changes and strong sign conflicts (e.g. landmark_00_local_dxy has 6 sign changes and 4 strong sign conflicts; landmark_00_local_cxy has 9 sign changes and 14 strong sign conflicts), and relative node RMSE is often large (up to 0.997). A constant rule and a time-conditioned rule therefore cannot be distinguished from these curves alone, and the curves are contrasts, not absolute reward targets.

The curve-fidelity audit selected only 24 of the candidate curves under the rule relative_rmse_le 0.35, strong_sign_conflict_nodes_eq 0, quiet_node_large_fit_fraction_le 0.1, absolute_integrated_z_ge 0.1, batch_direction_fraction_ge 0.857 and q_lt 0.05. For the audited curves, last-node empirical and fitted z frequently disagree in sign (e.g. landmark_00_occupancy3 empirical -0.040 vs fit 0.545; landmark_16_occupancy5 empirical 0.315 vs fit -0.175), and Legendre runtime use is disallowed. This limits how much temporal structure can be read from the fitted curves.

Turnover accounting separates population-contrast change from parent-child increment contrasts: for several features the edge (parent-child) rate and the turnover residual rate are large and opposite in sign to the population rate (e.g. landmark_00_local_cxx population -0.058, edge -4.343, residual 4.286; landmark_07_local_cyy population 0.863, edge -4.770, residual 5.633; landmark_16_local_cyy population 0.465, edge -5.903, residual 6.367). The residual is an accounting diagnostic that includes score reclassification and extant-parent weighting, not a causal selection effect or atom velocity.

Parent-child increment contrasts are mostly weak and inconsistent: shape_xx (-3.70, q 0.095), shape_yy (-3.85, q 0.161), shape_xz (3.00, q 0.207), pair_kernel_2.5 (3.96, q 0.208), pair_kernel_7.0 (-3.14, q 0.208), landmark_00_softmin (-4.91, q 0.046) and landmark_00_occupancy3 (4.28, q 0.081) are the larger magnitudes, but most features have wide confidence intervals spanning zero and positive batch fractions near 0.5. This does not support a strong within-path change claim.

Descendant survival credit is recorded joint-head credit, not decoded terminal affinity: survival_enrichment_z is positive for landmark_00_soft_mass (0.365, q 0.120), landmark_07_soft_mass (0.220, q 0.356), landmark_10_soft_mass (0.234, q 0.302) and landmark_18_local_czz (0.217, q 0.302), and negative for several local_czz and local_cyy features (e.g. landmark_05_local_czz -0.419, q 0.120; landmark_09_local_czz -0.390, q 0.120; landmark_16_local_cyy -0.317, q 0.219). Because decoded terminal learning labels are unavailable, last-record credit cannot be presented as final affinity benefit.

The information audit reports that the geometric nearest-teacher comparison under sparse salient fields versus Hungarian fixed-frame RMS is not the full score-weighted reward or its FLOWR Jacobian, that nonnegative excess distance is by construction rather than a causal affinity effect, and that teacher score correlations are observational and not a fitted or independently validated affinity predictor. Lineage support records 14 complete-survival batches, BH correction jointly over 400 survival field/measure tests, and 349 nodes with fewer than 3 ancestors and 531 with fewer than 6; terminal metadata show terminal score time 0.99 and state time 1.0 with one future resampling node per batch. Decoded terminal learning labels are unavailable, and the static teacher modes are last-learning-node forecasts, not actual final structures.

hypotheses.claim: A testable coordinate hypothesis is that the signed favorable-minus-comparison contrast is carried mainly by short-range pair-distance shell densities (1.5-5.0 A) and by reduced shape_yy/shape_xx anisotropy, with the observable being the standardized pair_kernel and shape features, the intended response being a positive signed contrast on those features, the target origin being the observed selection nodes, and the spatial scale being the 1.5-5.0 A pair shells and the landmark radius 5.0 A. A discriminating failure condition would be a sign reversal of the pair_kernel_1.5-5.0 contrasts or of shape_yy under independent batches. Whether a permitted reward recipe can express this depends on the executing pointcloud scalar, which has no pair-kernel or moment term, so the hypothesis may remain descriptive.

A testable temporal hypothesis is that a time-conditioned regional attention rule would differ from a constant rule only where the observed-node contrast curves show reproducible sign changes without strong sign conflicts and with relative node RMSE below the audit threshold. The observable would be the validated absolute contrast at actual score nodes, the intended response a change in regional attention weight, the target origin the observed score nodes, and the temporal scale the observed window [0.0, 0.49]. A discriminating failure condition would be that the selected curves' last-node empirical and fitted signs disagree or that the sign conflicts exceed the audit threshold, in which case the temporal rule remains unsupported.

A testable accounting hypothesis is that the large turnover residual rates for local_cxx and local_cyy features reflect changing cohort composition and score reclassification rather than within-path coordinate change, because the edge rates and residuals are large and opposite in sign to the population rates. The observable would be the population, edge and residual rates, the intended response a decomposition of the population change, the target origin the parent-child edges, and the temporal scale the observed window. A discriminating failure condition would be a residual that is small relative to the edge rate, which would instead support within-path change. The residual is an accounting diagnostic, not a causal selection effect.

A testable joint-geometry hypothesis is that reduced joint innovation and internal RMS, together with higher native alignment and teacher innovation-contrast alignment, mark regions that add information beyond common motion, while the negative association with observed child score gain marks a survivor-bias caveat. The observable would be the adjusted branch-covariance joint RMS and the within-selector alignment diagnostics, the intended response a change in joint-motion scale, the target origin the observed selection nodes, and the spatial scale the landmark radius 5.0 A. A discriminating failure condition would be a sign reversal of the joint RMS contrasts or of the alignment associations under independent batches.

A testable survival-credit hypothesis is that the positive survival enrichment for soft_mass at landmarks 00, 07 and 10 and for landmark_18_local_czz, and the negative enrichment for several local_czz and local_cyy features, reflect selection enrichment rather than final affinity benefit. The observable would be the recorded joint-head survival credit, the intended response a change in survival enrichment, the target origin the observed selection nodes, and the temporal scale the observed window. A discriminating failure condition would be decoded terminal labels that reverse the sign of the survival enrichment; because decoded terminal learning labels are unavailable, this comparison cannot be made and the hypothesis remains descriptive.

A testable increment hypothesis is that the parent-child increment contrasts for shape_xx, shape_yy, shape_xz, pair_kernel_2.5, pair_kernel_7.0, landmark_00_softmin and landmark_00_occupancy3 are too weak and inconsistent to support a within-path change claim, and that the larger turnover residuals instead point to changing cohort composition. The observable would be the increment integrated rate z and the turnover residual, the intended response a decomposition of within-path versus cohort change, the target origin the parent-child edges, and the temporal scale the observed window. A discriminating failure condition would be a consistent sign and narrow confidence interval for the increment contrasts across independent batches.

limitations: Descendant credit is recorded joint-head credit, not decoded terminal affinity; decoded terminal learning labels are unavailable.
Turnover residual includes score reclassification and extant-parent weighting, not only resampling.
Adjusted branch covariance is supplied evidence; region moments themselves are not rigid-motion residuals.
Curve fitting does not establish causal benefit or a gradient; no time bins or outside-window analysis.
Static teachers are last-learning-node forecasts, not actual final structures.
All weak and null scalar effects retained; current study outcomes are withheld from design roles.
The executing pointcloud scalar has no pair-kernel, moment, joint-motif or geometry-block term, so several supported contrasts may remain descriptive.
Temperatures are immutable task parameters and no temperature edit is proposed.
